title.zh: 卷二百五十二 列傳第十一 王景 王晏 郭從義 李洪信 武行德 楊承信 侯章
title.en: Volume 252 Biographies 11: Wang Jing, Wang Yan, Guo Congyi, Li Hongxin, Wu Xingde, Yang Chengxin, Hou Zhang
title.raw: 卷二百五十二 列傳第十一 王景 王晏 郭從義 李洪信 武行德 楊承信 侯章 Volume 252 Biographies 11: Wang Jing, Wang Yan, Guo Congyi, Li Hongxin, Wu Xingde, Yang Chengxin, Hou Zhang

sentences.zh: 王景，萊州掖人，家世力田。

translations.literal: Wang Jing was a native of Ye in Laizhou; his family for generations tilled the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing came from Ye in Laizhou. For generations his family had been farmers.

sentences.zh: 景少倜儻，善騎射，不事生業，結里中惡少為群盜。

translations.literal: When young Jing was free-spirited and bold, skilled at riding and archery, did not pursue a livelihood, and joined the neighborhood ruffians to become a band of robbers.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Wang Jing was bold and unrestrained, skilled in horsemanship and archery. He neglected honest work and banded with local rowdies to become a gang of brigands.

sentences.zh: 梁大將王檀鎮滑臺，以景隸麾下，與後唐莊宗戰河上，檀有功，景嘗左右之。

translations.literal: The Liang general Wang Tan garrisoned Huatai and placed Jing under his command. He fought the Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong on the Yellow River; Tan had merit, and Jing often assisted at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Liang general Wang Tan held Huatai and took Jing into his service. When Tan fought the Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong along the Yellow River, Tan won credit in battle and Jing often fought at his side.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入汴，景來降，累遷奉聖都虞候。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Jing came to surrender and was repeatedly promoted to Chief Commandant of the Fengsheng Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong entered Bian, Jing surrendered and rose through successive appointments to Chief Commandant of the Fengsheng Guard.

sentences.zh: 清泰末，從張敬達圍晉陽，會契丹來援，景以所部歸晉祖。

translations.literal: At the end of the Qingtai era he followed Zhang Jingda in besieging Jinyang. When the Khitans came to the rescue, Jing brought his command over to the Later Jin founder.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Qingtai reign he followed Zhang Jingda in the siege of Jinyang. When the Khitans marched to relieve the city, Jing defected with his troops to the Later Jin founder.

sentences.zh: 天福初，授相州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianfu era he was appointed Prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianfu reign he was made Prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 范延光據鄴叛，屬郡多為所脅從，景獨分兵拒守，晉祖嘉之，遷耀州團練使。

translations.literal: When Fan Yanguang seized Ye and rebelled, many subordinate prefectures were compelled to follow him, but Jing alone divided his troops to resist and hold firm. The Later Jin founder praised this and transferred him to be Militia Commissioner of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yanguang rebelled and held Ye, most neighboring prefectures were forced to join him, but Jing alone sent detachments to resist and hold his ground. The Later Jin founder commended him and appointed him Militia Commissioner of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 及代，會晉祖幸鄴，留為京城巡檢使，改洺州團練使。

translations.literal: When the dynasty changed, as the Later Jin founder visited Ye, Jing was left behind as Capital Patrol Commissioner and then made Militia Commissioner of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the change of dynasty, while the Later Jin founder was visiting Ye, Jing was left in the capital as Patrol Commissioner and later transferred to Militia Commissioner of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 開運初，授侍衛馬軍左廂都校。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaiyun era he was appointed Commander of the Left Wing of the Palace Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyun reign he was appointed Commander of the Left Wing of the Palace Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 二年，契丹南侵，少帝幸澶淵，景與高行周等大破契丹眾於戚城，遷侍衛馬軍都指揮使、領鄭州防禦使，出為晉州巡檢使、知州事，拜橫海軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year the Khitans invaded south. The young emperor went to Chanyuan. Jing, together with Gao Xingzhou and others, routed the Khitan forces at Qi City. He was promoted to Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Cavalry while holding the post of Defender of Zhengzhou, then sent out as Patrol Commissioner of Jinzhou and Acting Prefect, and finally enfeoffed as Military Governor of the Henghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the reign the Khitans invaded from the north. The young emperor went to Chanyuan. Jing joined Gao Xingzhou and others in a great victory over the Khitans at Qi City. He was promoted to Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Cavalry and Defender of Zhengzhou, then sent out as Patrol Commissioner and acting prefect of Jinzhou, and finally enfeoffed as Military Governor of Henghai.

sentences.zh: 契丹至汴，以其黨代景。

translations.literal: When the Khitans reached Bian, they replaced Jing with one of their own partisans.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans reached Bian, they replaced him with one of their own men.

sentences.zh: 景歸次常山，聞契丹主殂欒城，即間道歸鎮，斬關而入，契丹遁去。

translations.literal: Jing halted at Changshan. Hearing that the Khitan ruler had died at Luancheng, he took a bypath back to his commandery, cut through the passes to enter, and the Khitans fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Jing paused at Changshan. When he heard that the Khitan emperor had died at Luancheng, he took a hidden route back to his post, forced the passes open, and entered; the Khitans withdrew.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐初，加同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyou era of Han he was given the additional title of Co-Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianyou reign of Later Han he was made Co-Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 會契丹饑，幽州民多度關求食，至滄州境者五千餘人，景善懷撫，詔給田處之。

translations.literal: When famine struck the Khitans, many people of Youzhou crossed the passes seeking food. More than five thousand reached the borders of Cangzhou. Jing treated them kindly and soothed them, and an edict granted them fields and settled them there.
translations.idiomatic: Famine among the Khitans drove many people of Youzhou across the passes in search of food. More than five thousand reached Cangzhou. Jing received them with kindness, and the court ordered fields allotted to settle them.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加守太保，封太原郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was given the additional title of Acting Grand Guardian and enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song dynasty he was made Acting Grand Guardian and enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年春來朝，太祖宴賜加等，復以為鳳翔節度、西面緣邊都部署。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Jianlong he came to court. Taizu feasted and rewarded him with added honors, then again appointed him Military Governor of Fengxiang and Overall Frontier Commander of the Western Marches.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Jianlong he came to court. Taizu entertained him with a feast and added honors, then reappointed him Military Governor of Fengxiang and Overall Commander of the Western Frontier.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，追封岐王，謚元靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title Grand Tutor, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, and granted the posthumous name Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, and given the posthumous name Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 初，景之奔晉也，妻坐戮，二子逃獲免。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jing had fled to Jin, his wife was executed by association, and his two sons escaped and were spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing had first defected to Later Jin, his wife was executed for his crime, but his two sons escaped and survived.

sentences.zh: 晉祖待之厚，賞賜萬計，嘗問景所欲，對曰：「臣自歸國，受恩隆厚，誠無所欲。

translations.literal: The Later Jin founder treated him generously, with rewards numbering in the tens of thousands. He once asked Jing what he desired. Jing replied, "Since I returned to the state I have received profound favor and truly desire nothing."
translations.idiomatic: The Later Jin founder treated him with great generosity, rewarding him lavishly on countless occasions. Once he asked what Jing wanted. Jing answered, "Since I came over to Your Majesty I have received such deep favor that I truly want nothing."

sentences.zh: 」固問之，景稽顙再拜曰：「臣昔為卒，嘗負胡床從隊長出入，屢過官妓侯小師家，意甚慕之。

translations.literal: " When pressed again, Jing bowed his forehead to the ground and said again, "When I was once a soldier I used to carry a folding chair and follow my squad leader in and out, and often passed the house of the official courtesan Hou Xiaoshi. I greatly admired her."
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor pressed him again, Jing kowtowed and said, "When I was a common soldier I used to carry a camp stool for my squad leader and often passed the house of the official courtesan Hou Xiaoshi. I admired her greatly."

sentences.zh: 今妻被誅，誠得小師為妻足矣。

translations.literal: Now that my wife has been executed, if I could truly have Xiaoshi as my wife that would be enough."
translations.idiomatic: Now that my wife has been put to death, if I could have Xiaoshi for my wife, that would be enough."

sentences.zh: 」晉祖大笑，即以小師賜景。

translations.literal: " The Later Jin founder laughed loudly and at once bestowed Xiaoshi upon Jing.
translations.idiomatic: " The Later Jin founder laughed heartily and at once gave him Hou Xiaoshi.

sentences.zh: 景甚寵嬖之，後累封楚國夫人。

translations.literal: Jing greatly favored and doted on her, and she was later repeatedly ennobled as Lady of the State of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Jing cherished her deeply, and she was later raised in rank to Lady of the State of Chu.

sentences.zh: 侯氏嘗盜景金數百兩，私遺舊人，景知而不責。

translations.literal: The Hou clan woman once stole several hundred taels of Jing's gold and secretly gave them to old acquaintances. Jing knew but did not punish her.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Hou once stole several hundred taels of his gold and secretly gave them to old friends. Jing knew of it but did not reproach her.

sentences.zh: 性謙退，折節下士，每朝廷使至，雖卑位必降階送迎，周旋盡禮。

translations.literal: By nature he was modest and retiring, lowering himself to honor scholars. Whenever an envoy from court arrived, even if of humble rank he would descend the steps to welcome and send him off, observing every courtesy in his dealings.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was modest and unassuming, treating men of learning with deference. Whenever an envoy from court arrived, no matter how low his rank, Jing would go down the steps to welcome and escort him, observing every point of ceremony.

sentences.zh: 左右或曰：「王位尊崇，無自謙抑。

translations.literal: Those around him sometimes said, "Your princely rank is exalted; there is no need to humble yourself."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants sometimes said, "Your rank as prince is exalted. You need not humble yourself so."

sentences.zh: 」景曰：「人臣重君命，固當如是，我惟恐不謹耳。

translations.literal: " Jing said, "As subjects we honor the ruler's command and ought by rights to act thus. I only fear that I am not careful enough."
translations.idiomatic: " Jing replied, "A subject who honors the ruler's commission ought to act in just this way. I only fear that I am not careful enough."

sentences.zh: 」初封郡王，朝廷以吏部尚書張昭將命，景尤加禮重，以萬餘緡遺昭。

translations.literal: " When he was first enfeoffed as Prince of a Commandery, the court sent Zhang Zhao, Minister of Personnel, to convey the commission. Jing showed him exceptional courtesy and presented Zhao with more than ten thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: " When he was first enfeoffed as a commandery prince, the court sent Zhang Zhao, Minister of Personnel, to invest him. Jing treated him with exceptional respect and gave him more than ten thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 左右或言其過厚，景曰：「我在行伍間，即聞張尚書名，今使於我，是朝廷厚我也，豈可以往例為限耶？」

translations.literal: Those around him said the gift was excessive. Jing said, "Even when I was in the ranks I had heard Minister Zhang's name. That he is now envoy to me shows that the court honors me. How can I be bound by former precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said the gift was too lavish. Jing said, "Even when I was in the ranks I had heard of Minister Zhang. That the court sends him to me is a mark of honor. How can I be limited by ordinary precedent?"

sentences.zh: 景子廷義、廷睿、廷訓。

translations.literal: Jing's sons were Tingyi, Tingrui, and Tingxun.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's sons were Tingyi, Tingrui, and Tingxun.

sentences.zh: 廷訓至驍衛大將軍致仕。

translations.literal: Tingxun rose to Grand General of the Valiant Guard and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxun rose to Grand General of the Valiant Guard and then retired.

sentences.zh: 廷義起家供奉官，改如京副使，以善騎射，周世宗擢為虎捷都虞候，遷龍捷右第二軍都校、領珍州刺史。

translations.literal: Tingyi began as a Palace Attendant, then became Vice Commissioner for the Capital. Because he was skilled at riding and archery, the Later Zhou Emperor Shizong promoted him to Chief Commandant of the Tiger Swift Guard, then transferred him to Commander of the Second Army of the Right Dragon Swift Guard while holding the post of Prefect of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyi began as a Palace Attendant and became Vice Commissioner for the Capital. Skilled in horsemanship and archery, he was promoted by Later Zhou Shizong to Chief Commandant of the Tiger Swift Guard, then made Commander of the Second Army of the Right Dragon Swift Guard and Prefect of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋初，改內外馬步軍副都軍頭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was made Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Inner and Outer Horse and Foot Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was appointed Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Inner and Outer Horse and Foot Armies.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，與韓重贇率師護治滑州靈河新堤。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiande he joined Han Chongyun in leading troops to oversee repair of the new embankment on the Ling River at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qiande he joined Han Chongyun in leading troops to repair the new Ling River embankment at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，增治京城，又命廷義董其役。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the capital was enlarged and repaired, and Tingyi was again ordered to supervise the work.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the capital was expanded and repaired, and Tingyi was again put in charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，加領橫州團練使，從征太原。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he was additionally appointed Militia Commissioner of Hengzhou and followed the campaign against Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he was also made Militia Commissioner of Hengzhou and took part in the campaign against Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 廷義性勇敢，親鼓士乘城，獨免胄，矢中其腦而顛，經宿卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: Tingyi was brave by nature. He personally roused the men to mount the wall, alone removed his helmet, was struck in the head by an arrow and fell, and died after a night, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyi was naturally courageous. He personally rallied the men onto the walls, alone removed his helmet, was struck in the head by an arrow and fell, and died the next day at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚惜之，優詔贈建雄軍節度。

translations.literal: Taizu deeply regretted it and by gracious edict posthumously granted him the post of Military Governor of the Jianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu deeply mourned his loss and by gracious edict posthumously made him Military Governor of Jianxiong.

sentences.zh: 廷睿性驕傲，好夸誕，每言：「我當代王景之子。

translations.literal: Tingrui was proud by nature and fond of boastful exaggeration. He often said, "I am the successor to Wang Jing's sons."
translations.idiomatic: Tingrui was arrogant and fond of grandiose boasts. He often said, "I am the successor to Wang Jing's sons."

sentences.zh: 」聞者咸笑之，因目為『王當代』。

translations.literal: " All who heard laughed at him, and so he was nicknamed "Wang the Successor."
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone who heard him laughed, and people nicknamed him "Wang the Successor."

sentences.zh: 王晏，徐州滕人，家世力田。

translations.literal: Wang Yan was a native of Teng in Xuzhou; his family for generations tilled the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan came from Teng in Xuzhou. For generations his family had been farmers.

sentences.zh: 晏少壯勇無賴，嘗率群寇行攻劫。

translations.literal: When young Yan was strong, fierce, and unruly, and once led a band of raiders in attacks and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Wang Yan was strong, fierce, and lawless, and once led a band of raiders on attacks and plunder.

sentences.zh: 梁末，徐方大亂，屬邑皆為他盜所剽，惟晏鄉里恃晏獲全。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang, the Xu region fell into great disorder. Subordinate districts were all plundered by other bandits, but Yan's home village alone relied on Yan and was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Later Liang, the Xu region fell into chaos. Neighboring districts were plundered by other bandits, but Yan's home village alone was spared because it relied on him.

sentences.zh: 後唐同光中，應募隸禁軍，累遷奉國小校。

translations.literal: In the Tongguang era of Later Tang he answered the call and entered the Palace Guard, rising through successive promotions to Junior Officer of the Fengguo Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongguang reign of Later Tang he enlisted in the Palace Guard and rose to Junior Officer of the Fengguo Guard.

sentences.zh: 晉開運末，與本軍都校趙暉、忠衛都校侯章等戍陜州。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyun era of Jin he garrisoned Shaanzhou together with the Commander of his army Zhao Hui, the Commander of the Loyal Guard Hou Zhang, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Kaiyun reign of Later Jin he was posted to Shaanzhou with his army commander Zhao Hui, Loyal Guard commander Hou Zhang, and others.

sentences.zh: 會契丹至汴，遣其將劉愿據陜，恣行暴虐，晏與暉等謀曰：「今契丹南侵，天下洶洶，英雄豪傑固當乘時自奮。

translations.literal: When the Khitans reached Bian they sent their general Liu Yuan to hold Shaan and indulged in violence and cruelty. Yan and Hui and the others plotted, saying, "Now the Khitans invade south and the realm is in turmoil. Heroes and great men ought by rights to seize the moment and rouse themselves."
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans reached Bian they sent their general Liu Yuan to hold Shaan, where he ruled with violence and cruelty. Yan and Hui plotted together, saying, "The Khitans are invading from the north and the realm is in turmoil. Men of talent ought to seize the moment and rise."

sentences.zh: 且聞太原劉公威德遠被，人心歸服，若殺愿送款河東，為天下倡首，則取富貴如反掌耳。

translations.literal: Moreover we hear that Lord Liu of Taiyuan's prestige and virtue reach far and men's hearts turn to him. If we kill Yuan and offer allegiance to Hedong, taking the lead for the realm, then winning wealth and honor will be like turning the hand."
translations.idiomatic: We hear that Lord Liu of Taiyuan's fame and virtue reach far and that the people look to him. If we kill Yuan and submit to Hedong, taking the lead for the realm, wealth and honor will be ours in an instant."

sentences.zh: 」暉等然之。

translations.literal: " Hui and the others agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 晏乃率敢死士數人夜踰城，入府署，劫庫兵給其徒，遲明，斬愿首級府門外。

translations.literal: Yan then led several dare-to-die men, scaled the wall by night, entered the government compound, seized weapons from the arsenal to arm his followers, and at dawn cut off Yuan's head and displayed it outside the compound gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yan led a handful of dare-to-die men over the wall by night, entered the government compound, seized arms from the arsenal for his followers, and at dawn cut off Yuan's head and displayed it outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 眾請暉為帥，章為本城副指揮使、內外巡檢使兼都虞候；

translations.literal: The men asked that Hui be commander, Zhang be Deputy Commander of the local garrison, Inner and Outer Patrol Commissioner, and also Chief Commandant;
translations.idiomatic: The troops asked that Hui be commander and Zhang Deputy Commander of the garrison, Inner and Outer Patrol Commissioner, and Chief Commandant;

sentences.zh: 遣其子漢倫奉表晉陽。

translations.literal: and sent his son Hanlun to present a memorial at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: and sent his son Hanlun to present a memorial at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 時漢祖雖建號，威聲未振，得晏等來歸，甚喜，即日以暉為保平軍節度，章為鎮國軍節度，晏為絳州防禦使，仍領舊職。

translations.literal: At that time, though the Later Han founder had established his title, his prestige had not yet risen. Receiving Yan and the others in submission, he was greatly pleased. That very day he made Hui Military Governor of the Baoping Army, Zhang Military Governor of the Zhenguo Army, and Yan Defender of Jiangzhou while retaining his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Later Han founder had already proclaimed his reign, his authority was not yet secure. When Yan and the others submitted, he was delighted. That same day he made Hui Military Governor of Baoping, Zhang Military Governor of Zhenguo, and Yan Defender of Jiangzhou while keeping his former post.

sentences.zh: 既而暉等表晏始謀功為第一，遷建雄軍節度。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Hui and the others memorialized that Yan had been first in the original plot and ranked his merit first, and he was transferred to Military Governor of the Jianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Hui and the others reported that Yan had conceived the plot and ranked his merit first, and he was transferred to Military Governor of Jianxiong.

sentences.zh: 漢祖入汴，加同平章事。

translations.literal: When the Later Han founder entered Bian, Yan was given the additional title of Co-Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Han founder entered Bian, Yan was made Co-Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 初，晏至鎮，悉召故時同為盜者遺以金帛，從容置酒語之曰：「吾鄉素多盜，我與諸君昔嘗為之。

translations.literal: When Yan first reached his commandery he summoned all who had once been bandits with him, gave them gold and silks, set out wine at leisure, and said to them, "Our district has always had many bandits, and I with you gentlemen once did this ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: When Yan first took up his post he summoned all his former fellow bandits, gave them gold and silks, and over wine said calmly, "Our district has always had many bandits, and I once did the same with you."

sentences.zh: 後來者固當出諸君之下，為我告諭，令不復為，若不能改，吾必盡滅其族。

translations.literal: Those who come later ought by rights to rank below you gentlemen. Tell them for me to do it no more. If they cannot reform, I shall exterminate their clans to the last."
translations.idiomatic: Those who come after ought to defer to you. Tell them for me to stop. If they will not change, I shall exterminate their families to the last man."

sentences.zh: 」由是境內安靜，吏民詣闕舉留，請為晏立衣錦碑。

translations.literal: " From this the territory within his borders grew quiet. Officials and people went to court to praise him and ask that he be retained, requesting that a "return in brocade" stele be erected for Yan.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on his territory was at peace. Officials and commoners went to court to praise him and ask that he be retained, and requested a stele commemorating his return in glory.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，復請立德政碑。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign they again requested that a stele of virtuous governance be erected.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shizong's reign they again asked for a stele commemorating his virtuous rule.

sentences.zh: 世宗命比部郎中、知制誥張正撰文賜之，詔改其鄉里為使相鄉勳德里，私門立戟。

translations.literal: Shizong ordered Zhang Zheng, Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Drafter of Imperial Edicts, to compose the text and bestow it. An edict changed his home village to Merit Lane in Envoy-Minister Village and ordered halberds set up at his private gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong ordered Zhang Zheng, Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Drafter of Imperial Edicts, to compose the inscription. An edict renamed his home village Merit Lane in Envoy-Minister Village and granted halberds at his private gate.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改河南尹、西京留守。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to be Governor of Henan and Western Capital Regent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Governor of Henan and Regent of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年，移鳳翔節度。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande he was transferred to Military Governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiande he was transferred to Military Governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 六年，從世宗北征，為益津關一路馬軍都部署，韓令坤副焉，遂平三關。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Shizong on the northern campaign as Overall Commander of Cavalry for the Yijin Pass route, with Han Lingkun as his deputy, and thereby pacified the Three Passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he followed Shizong on the northern campaign as Overall Cavalry Commander for the Yijin Pass route, with Han Lingkun as his deputy, and helped secure the Three Passes.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，進封趙國公。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Yan was advanced in rank and enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Yan was promoted and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 從征李筠，師還，改安遠軍節度。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Li Jun, and when the army returned he was made Military Governor of the Anyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign against Li Jun, and when the army returned he was made Military Governor of Anyuan.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年，進封韓國公，上章請老，拜太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiande he was advanced and enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Han, submitted a memorial requesting retirement, and was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qiande he was promoted to Duke of Han, asked to retire, and was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent before leaving office.

sentences.zh: 每朝會，令綴中書門下班。

translations.literal: At each court assembly he was ordered to take his place at the end of the Zhongshu Gate shift.
translations.idiomatic: At each court assembly he was placed at the end of the Zhongshu Gate line.

sentences.zh: 俄歸洛陽別墅。

translations.literal: Before long he returned to his villa in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he retired to his villa in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year he died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year he died at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 廢朝三日，贈中書令。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for three days, and he was posthumously given the title Chief Councillor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning lasted three days, and he was posthumously honored as Chief Councillor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，晏為軍校，與平陸人王興善，其妻亦相為娣姒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yan was an army officer, he was on good terms with Wang Xing of Pinglu, and their wives were also sisters-in-law to each other.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was still an army officer he was close friends with Wang Xing of Pinglu, and their wives were sisters-in-law.

sentences.zh: 晏既貴，乃薄興，興不能平。

translations.literal: After Yan grew eminent he treated Xing coldly, and Xing could not be reconciled.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan rose to prominence he treated Xing coldly, and Xing could not accept it.

sentences.zh: 晏妻病，興語人曰：「吾能治之。

translations.literal: When Yan's wife fell ill, Xing told others, "I can cure her."
translations.idiomatic: When Yan's wife fell ill, Xing told people, "I can cure her."

sentences.zh: 」晏遽訪興，興曰：「我非能醫，但以公在陜時止一妻，今妓妾甚眾，得非待糟糠之薄，致夫人怏怏成疾耶？

translations.literal: " Yan hurried to visit Xing. Xing said, "I am not able to practice medicine, but when you, sir, were at Shaan you had only one wife. Now your singing girls and concubines are very many. Could it not be that treating your wife of humble days with coldness has made the lady discontented and brought on her illness?"
translations.idiomatic: " Yan hurried to see him. Xing said, "I am no physician, but when you were at Shaan you had only one wife. Now you have many singing girls and concubines. Could it be that neglecting the wife who shared your hardships has made her ill with resentment?"

sentences.zh: 若能斥去女侍，夫人之疾可立愈。

translations.literal: If you can drive away the female attendants, the lady's illness can be cured at once."
translations.idiomatic: If you dismiss your female attendants, your wife's illness will clear at once."

sentences.zh: 」晏以為謗己，乃誣以他事，悉案誅其夫妻。

translations.literal: " Yan took this as slander against himself, then framed them on other charges and had both husband and wife investigated and executed.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan took this as an insult, framed them on other charges, and had husband and wife executed after investigation.

sentences.zh: 守西洛日，白重贊鎮河陽，時世宗征淮南，重贊慮幷人乘間為寇，因葺城壘，且約晏為援。

translations.literal: While holding the Western Capital, Bai Chongzan garrisoned Heyang. At that time Shizong was campaigning in Huainan. Chongzan feared that the Bing region people might seize the opportunity to raid, and therefore repaired the walls and ramparts and also arranged with Yan as reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: While Yan held the Western Capital, Bai Chongzan was posted at Heyang. Shizong was campaigning in Huainan, and Chongzan feared that the Bing people might raid while he was away, so he repaired the fortifications and asked Yan for support.

sentences.zh: 晏意欲兼有三城，即與漢倫同率兵赴之。

translations.literal: Yan intended to take all three cities for himself and at once led troops with Hanlun to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Yan hoped to seize all three cities for himself and marched with Hanlun to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 重贊聞其來，拒不納，遣人語之曰：「公在陜州已立大功，河陽小城不煩枉駕。

translations.literal: Chongzan heard that he was coming, refused to admit him, and sent someone to tell him, "You, sir, already achieved great merit at Shaanzhou. This small city of Heyang does not require the trouble of your coming in person."
translations.idiomatic: Chongzan heard he was coming, refused him entry, and sent word, "You have already won great merit at Shaanzhou. This little city of Heyang does not require your personal visit."

sentences.zh: 」慚不能對，遂引兵還。

translations.literal: " Ashamed, he could not reply and therefore led his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: " Ashamed, he had no reply and withdrew his troops.

sentences.zh: 郭從義

translations.literal: Guo Congyi
translations.idiomatic: Guo Congyi

sentences.zh: 郭從義，其先沙陀部人。

translations.literal: Guo Congyi: his ancestors were people of the Shatuo tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Congyi's ancestors were of the Shatuo tribe.

sentences.zh: 父紹古，事後唐武皇忠謹，特見信任，賜姓李氏。

translations.literal: His father Shaogu served the Later Tang Martial Emperor with loyalty and care and was especially trusted, and was granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaogu served the Later Tang Martial Emperor with loyal devotion, won exceptional trust, and was granted the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 紹古卒，從義才丱角，莊宗畜於宮中，與諸子齒。

translations.literal: When Shaogu died, Congyi was still a child in his early years. Zhuangzong reared him in the palace and ranked him with his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: After Shaogu died, Congyi was still a small child. Zhuangzong raised him in the palace and treated him as one of his own sons.

sentences.zh: 明宗與紹古同事武皇，情好款狎，即位，以從義補內職，累遷內園使。

translations.literal: Mingzong and Shaogu had both served the Martial Emperor together and were on intimate friendly terms. When Mingzong took the throne he appointed Congyi to an inner palace post and promoted him through successive ranks to Commissioner of the Inner Gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong and Shaogu had served the Martial Emperor together and were close friends. When Mingzong took the throne he gave Congyi an inner palace post and eventually made him Commissioner of the Inner Gardens.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，始復姓郭氏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianfu era of Jin he first restored the surname Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianfu reign of Later Jin he resumed the surname Guo.

sentences.zh: 坐事出為宿州團練副使。

translations.literal: Because of an offense he was sent out as Deputy Militia Commissioner of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After an offense he was sent out as Deputy Militia Commissioner of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱北歸，遂家太原。

translations.literal: When his mother died he returned north and thereafter made his home in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he returned north and settled in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 漢祖在鎮，表為馬步軍都虞候，屢率師破破契丹於代北，及建大號，從義首贊其謀，擢鄭州防禦使，充東南道行營都虞候，領首軍自太行路渡河。

translations.literal: While the Later Han founder was in his commandery he memorialized that Congyi be made Chief Commandant of the Horse and Foot Armies. He repeatedly led troops to defeat the Khitans north of Dai. When the great title was established, Congyi was first to support his plans. He was promoted to Defender of Zhengzhou, made Chief Commandant of the Southeastern Route Army, and led the vanguard across the Yellow River by the Taihang route.
translations.idiomatic: While the Later Han founder held his post, he recommended Congyi as Chief Commandant of the Horse and Foot Armies. Congyi repeatedly led troops to defeat the Khitans north of Dai. When the founder proclaimed his reign, Congyi was the first to support his plans. He was promoted to Defender of Zhengzhou, made Chief Commandant of the Southeastern Route Army, and led the vanguard across the Yellow River by the Taihang route.

sentences.zh: 漢祖入汴，以為河北都巡檢使。

translations.literal: When the Later Han founder entered Bian, Congyi was made Overall Patrol Commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Han founder entered Bian, Congyi was appointed Overall Patrol Commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 杜重威據大名叛，以為行營諸軍都虞候，重威降，為鎮寧軍節度。

translations.literal: When Du Chongwei seized Daming and rebelled, Congyi was made Chief Commandant of All Armies of the Field Headquarters. When Chongwei surrendered, Congyi was made Military Governor of the Zhenning Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Chongwei rebelled and held Daming, Congyi was made Chief Commandant of All Armies of the Field Headquarters. After Chongwei surrendered, Congyi was made Military Governor of Zhenning.

sentences.zh: 趙思綰之叛，為行營都部署，賜戎裝、器仗、金帶。

translations.literal: When Zhao Sihuan rebelled, Congyi was made Overall Commander of the Field Headquarters and was granted military dress, weapons, and a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhao Sihuan's rebellion he was made Overall Commander of the Field Headquarters and granted military dress, arms, and a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 師至永興，圍其城，即以從義為永興軍節度。

translations.literal: When the army reached Yongxing and besieged its city, Congyi was at once made Military Governor of the Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Yongxing and besieged the city, Congyi was at once made Military Governor of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 思綰糧盡，城中人相食，從義繫書矢上，射入城中，說思綰令降，仍表於朝廷，許以華州節制。

translations.literal: When Sihuan's grain was exhausted the people within the city ate one another. Congyi tied a letter to an arrow, shot it into the city, and urged Sihuan to surrender. He also memorialized the court, offering him control of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Sihuan's supplies ran out the people in the city resorted to cannibalism. Congyi tied a letter to an arrow, shot it into the city, and urged him to surrender. He also memorialized the court, offering him the Huazhou command.

sentences.zh: 隱帝從其計，即遣使諭思綰，思綰開門納款。

translations.literal: The Hidden Emperor followed his plan and at once sent envoys to instruct Sihuan. Sihuan opened the gates and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yindi accepted his plan and sent envoys to instruct Sihuan, who opened the gates and submitted.

sentences.zh: 翌日，從義具軍容入城，憩候館中，思綰入謁，即令武士執之，並其黨三百餘人悉斬於市，以功加同平章事。

translations.literal: The next day Congyi entered the city in full military array, rested in the reception lodge, and when Sihuan came to pay his respects he at once ordered warriors to seize him. Together with more than three hundred of his partisans they were all beheaded in the market. For this merit he was given the additional title of Co-Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Congyi entered the city in full military array and rested at the reception lodge. When Sihuan came to pay his respects, Congyi had warriors seize him. More than three hundred of his followers were beheaded in the market. For this achievement he was made Co-Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，加兼侍中，移鎮許州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangshun era of Zhou he was additionally made Palace Attendant and transferred to garrison Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangshun reign of Later Zhou he was also made Palace Attendant and transferred to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，親郊，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he personally performed the suburban sacrifice and was given the additional title of Acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiande he performed the suburban sacrifice in person and was made Acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 世宗將征劉崇，從義適來朝，因請扈從，世宗甚悅，改天平軍節度，即令從符彥卿破契丹於忻口。

translations.literal: When Shizong was about to campaign against Liu Chong, Congyi happened to come to court and therefore requested to follow in attendance. Shizong was greatly pleased, changed his post to Military Governor of the Tianping Army, and at once ordered him to follow Fu Yanqing in defeating the Khitans at Xinkou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong was about to campaign against Liu Chong, Congyi happened to be at court and asked to accompany him. Shizong was delighted, made him Military Governor of Tianping, and ordered him to join Fu Yanqing in defeating the Khitans at Xinkou.

sentences.zh: 師還，以功加兼中書令。

translations.literal: When the army returned, for his merit he was additionally made Chief Councillor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was also made Chief Councillor of the Central Secretariat for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 四年，從征淮南，移鎮徐州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the campaign in Huainan and was transferred to garrison Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he joined the Huainan campaign and was transferred to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 及世宗自迎鑾至泗州，見於行在。

translations.literal: When Shizong came from Yingluan to Sizhou, Congyi met him at the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong traveled from Yingluan to Sizhou, Congyi met him at the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，加開府階。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong took the throne, Congyi was given the rank of Opening the Government.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong took the throne, he was granted the rank of Opening the Government.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加守中書令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was given the additional title of Acting Chief Councillor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song dynasty he was made Acting Chief Councillor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太祖征揚州，從義迎謁於路，願扈從，不允。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against Yangzhou, Congyi met and paid his respects on the road and wished to follow in attendance, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu campaigned against Yangzhou, Congyi met him on the road and asked to accompany him, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，又為河中尹、護國國節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande he was again made Governor of Hezhong and Military Governor of the Huguo State.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande he was again made Governor of Hezhong and Military Governor of Huguo.

sentences.zh: 六年，以疾歸京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, because of illness he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he returned to the capital because of illness.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，改左金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he was changed to Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he was made Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 逾年，上章請老，拜太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: After more than a year he submitted a memorial requesting retirement and was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he asked to retire and was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent before leaving office.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年六十三，贈中書令。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged sixty-three, and was posthumously given the title Chief Councillor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died at the age of sixty-three and was posthumously honored as Chief Councillor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從義性重厚，有謀略，多技藝，尤善飛白書。

translations.literal: Congyi was grave and steady by nature, possessed strategy, had many skills, and was especially skilled at feibai calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi was grave and steady by nature, resourceful in counsel, skilled in many arts, and especially accomplished in feibai calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 初，思綰之叛也，巡檢使喬守溫遁去，姬妾悉入思綰，思綰敗，從義盡取之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sihuan rebelled, the Patrol Commissioner Qiao Shouwen fled away and his concubines all fell into Sihuan's hands. When Sihuan was defeated, Congyi took them all for himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Sihuan rebelled, Patrol Commissioner Qiao Shouwen fled, and his concubines all fell into Sihuan's hands. After Sihuan's defeat, Congyi took them all for himself.

sentences.zh: 守溫詣從義求其愛妾，雖不敢拒，而心銜焉，遂發守溫逃遁事，坐棄市，人皆冤之。

translations.literal: Shouwen went to Congyi to ask for his favorite concubine back. Though he did not dare refuse, in his heart he harbored resentment, and therefore exposed Shouwen's flight. Shouwen was executed in the market, and all considered it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Shouwen came to ask for his favorite concubine. Though Congyi did not dare refuse outright, he bore a grudge and exposed Shouwen's flight. Shouwen was executed in the market, and everyone considered it unjust.

sentences.zh: 從義善擊毬，嘗侍太祖於便殿，命擊之。

translations.literal: Congyi was skilled at polo. Once he attended Taizu in the side hall and was ordered to play.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi was skilled at polo. Once in the side hall Taizu ordered him to play.

sentences.zh: 從義易衣跨驢，馳驟殿庭，周旋擊拂，曲盡其妙。

translations.literal: Congyi changed clothes, mounted a donkey, galloped through the palace courtyard, wheeled and struck, and brought out every subtlety of the art.
translations.idiomatic: He changed clothes, mounted a donkey, galloped through the palace courtyard, and played with such skill that every subtlety of the game was displayed.

sentences.zh: 既罷，上賜坐，謂之曰：「卿技固精矣，然非將相所為。

translations.literal: When he finished, the emperor granted him a seat and said to him, "Your skill is indeed refined, yet this is not what generals and ministers ought to do."
translations.idiomatic: When he finished, the emperor gave him a seat and said, "Your skill is indeed fine, but this is not what a general or minister ought to do."

sentences.zh: 」從義大慚。

translations.literal: " Congyi was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: " Congyi was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 子守忠、守信。

translations.literal: His sons were Shouzhong and Shouxin.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shouzhong and Shouxin.

sentences.zh: 守忠至閑廄副使。

translations.literal: Shouzhong rose to Deputy Commissioner of the Leisure Stables.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong rose to Deputy Commissioner of the Leisure Stables.

sentences.zh: 守信字寶臣，頗知書，與士大夫遊，至東上閣門使、知邢州，卒。

translations.literal: Shouxin, style name Baochen, was quite learned in books, associated with scholar-officials, rose to Commissioner of the Eastern Upper Gate and Acting Prefect of Xingzhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxin, style name Baochen, was well read, kept company with scholar-officials, rose to Commissioner of the Eastern Upper Gate and Acting Prefect of Xingzhou, and died.

sentences.zh: 子世隆為比部員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Shilong was Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shilong served as Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 世隆子昭祐、承祐。

translations.literal: Shilong's sons were Zhaoyou and Chengyou.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong's sons were Zhaoyou and Chengyou.

sentences.zh: 昭祐為閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Zhaoyou was Attendant of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyou was Attendant of the Gate.

sentences.zh: 曾孫 承祐

translations.literal: Great-grandson Chengyou
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandson Chengyou

sentences.zh: 承祐，字天錫，娶舒王元偁女，授西頭供奉官。

translations.literal: Chengyou, style name Tiansi, married a daughter of Prince Shu Yuan Cheng and was appointed Western Head Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyou, style name Tiansi, married a daughter of Prince Shu Yuan Cheng and was appointed Western Head Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 仁宗為皇太子，承祐補左清道率府率、春坊左謁者，真宗為玉石小牌二，勒銘為戒飭之。

translations.literal: When Renzong was Crown Prince, Chengyou was appointed Colonel of the Left Pure Way Command and Left Usher of the Eastern Palace. Zhenzong had two small jade plaques made and inscribed them as admonitions to discipline him.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was Crown Prince, Chengyou was made Colonel of the Left Pure Way Command and Left Usher of the Eastern Palace. Zhenzong had two small jade plaques inscribed as admonitions to keep him in line.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，遷西院副使兼閣道通事舍人、勾當翰林司，遷西上閣門副使。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Chengyou was transferred to Deputy Commissioner of the Western Court while also serving as Imperial Herald of the Gate Passage and Superintendent of the Hanlin Office, then promoted to Deputy Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, he was made Deputy Commissioner of the Western Court, also Imperial Herald of the Gate Passage and Superintendent of the Hanlin Office, then Deputy Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate.

sentences.zh: 坐盜御酒及用尚方金器除名，岳州編管，徙許州別駕。

translations.literal: Because he stole imperial wine and used gold vessels of the Imperial Workshop he was struck from the rolls, placed under registered supervision at Yuezhou, and transferred to be Vice Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For stealing imperial wine and using gold vessels from the Imperial Workshop he was dismissed, placed under supervision at Yuezhou, and transferred to Vice Governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 起為率府率，遷西京作坊使、勾當右騏驥院。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Colonel of the Commandery, then transferred to Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops and Superintendent of the Right Fine Horses Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Colonel of the Commandery, then made Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops and Superintendent of the Right Fine Horses Court.

sentences.zh: 院之大校試路馬者，前鳴鞭擁御蓋，承祐代試之，其狂僭如此。

translations.literal: When the chief instructor of the court tested road horses, runners cracked whips ahead and bore the imperial canopy. Chengyou substituted himself in the test — his arrogance and presumption were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: When the court's chief instructor tested road horses, whips were cracked ahead and the imperial canopy borne before him. Chengyou took the test in his place — such was his arrogance.

sentences.zh: 進六宅使、象州團練使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Commissioner of the Six Residences and Militia Commissioner of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Six Residences and Militia Commissioner of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 承祐性狡獪，緣東宮恩，又憑藉王邸親，既廢復用，廼僭言事，或指切人過失，同列謂之『武諫官』。

translations.literal: Chengyou was crafty and cunning by nature. Relying on favor from the Eastern Palace and also on kinship with the prince's household, after dismissal he was used again and then presumptuously spoke on state affairs, sometimes pointing out others' faults directly. His colleagues called him the "Military Remonstrator."
translations.idiomatic: Chengyou was crafty by nature. He relied on favor from the Eastern Palace and kinship with the prince's household. After dismissal he was restored and then presumptuously spoke on affairs of state, sometimes pointing out others' faults bluntly. His colleagues called him the "Military Remonstrator."

sentences.zh: 真授衛州刺史、知相州，入為群牧副使，改濰州團練使，歷知曹、鄭、澶、鄆、貝州。

translations.literal: He was formally appointed Prefect of Weizhou and Acting Prefect of Xiangzhou, entered service as Deputy Commissioner of the Herds, was changed to Militia Commissioner of Weizhou, and in succession served as acting prefect of Cao, Zheng, Chan, Yun, and Bei.
translations.idiomatic: He was formally appointed Prefect of Weizhou and Acting Prefect of Xiangzhou, then made Deputy Commissioner of the Herds, Militia Commissioner of Weizhou, and in turn acting prefect of Cao, Zheng, Chan, Yun, and Bei.

sentences.zh: 徙澶州兵馬總管，役卒有異謀者，廉得不待奏，捕斬之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Overall Commander of Chanzhou's horse and foot forces. When corvée laborers were found to harbor unusual plots, he investigated, obtained proof, and without awaiting memorial had them seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Overall Commander of Chanzhou's forces. When corvée laborers were found plotting sedition, he investigated, and without waiting for approval had them seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 再知澶州，會中使過，遽延入問管軍闕補何人，使者曰：「聞朝廷方擇才武者。

translations.literal: He again served as acting prefect of Chanzhou. When an imperial envoy passed through, he hurriedly invited him in and asked who would fill the vacant post overseeing the army. The envoy said, "I hear the court is now selecting men of talent and martial ability."
translations.idiomatic: He again served as acting prefect of Chanzhou. When an imperial envoy passed through, he hurriedly invited him in and asked who would fill the vacant army command post. The envoy said, "I hear the court is selecting men of talent and martial ability."

sentences.zh: 」承祐起挽彊自衒，左右皆笑。

translations.literal: " Chengyou rose, drew a strong bow to display himself, and those around him all laughed.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengyou rose, drew a strong bow to show off his strength, and everyone present laughed.

sentences.zh: 入為龍神衛四廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: He entered service as Commander-in-Chief of the Four Wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Four Wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard.

sentences.zh: 以父喪，起復真定府、定州等路副都總管。

translations.literal: When his father died he was recalled from mourning to serve as Deputy Overall Commander of the Zhending Prefecture and Dingzhou circuit routes.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he was recalled from mourning to serve as Deputy Overall Commander of the Zhending and Dingzhou routes.

sentences.zh: 諫官歐陽脩、余靖論其非才，改知相州，尋徙大名府副都總管。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials Ouyang Xiu and Yu Jing argued that he lacked ability and was changed to Acting Prefect of Xiangzhou, then soon transferred to Deputy Overall Commander of Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials Ouyang Xiu and Yu Jing argued that he lacked ability. He was made Acting Prefect of Xiangzhou, then soon transferred to Deputy Overall Commander of Daming.

sentences.zh: 樞密使杜衍惡承祐驕恣，奏罷軍權，為相州觀察使、永興軍副都總管，改知邢州，徙河陽兵馬總管。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Du Yan hated Chengyou's arrogance and willfulness, memorialized to remove his military authority, and made him Observation Commissioner of Xiangzhou and Deputy Overall Commander of the Yongxing Army, then changed him to Acting Prefect of Xingzhou and transferred him to Overall Commander of Heyang's horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Du Yan hated Chengyou's arrogance and had his military authority removed. He was made Observation Commissioner of Xiangzhou and Deputy Overall Commander of Yongxing, then Acting Prefect of Xingzhou, then Overall Commander of Heyang's forces.

sentences.zh: 衍去位，復進為殿前都虞候、幷代州副都總管兼知代州，徙邢州。

translations.literal: When Yan left his post, Chengyou was again advanced to Chief Commandant Before the Hall and Deputy Overall Commander of Bing and Daizhou while also Acting Prefect of Daizhou, then transferred to Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan left office, Chengyou was again promoted to Chief Commandant Before the Hall, Deputy Overall Commander of Bing and Daizhou and Acting Prefect of Daizhou, then transferred to Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 諫官錢明逸言承祐無廉守，邢民素厭苦之，改相州，徙秦鳳路副總管。

translations.literal: The remonstrance official Qian Mingyi said Chengyou lacked integrity in office and that the people of Xing had long been wearied and afflicted by him. He was changed to Xiangzhou and transferred to Deputy Overall Commander of the Qinfeng route.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Qian Mingyi said Chengyou lacked integrity and that the people of Xing had long suffered under him. He was transferred to Xiangzhou, then to Deputy Overall Commander of the Qinfeng route.

sentences.zh: 累遷建武軍節度使、殿前副都指揮使。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Military Governor of the Jianwu Army and Deputy Commander-in-Chief Before the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Military Governor of Jianwu and Deputy Commander-in-Chief Before the Hall.

sentences.zh: 尋以宣徽南院使判應天府，府壁壘不完，盜至卒無以禦，承祐始城南關，浚沙、濉、盟三河。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Southern Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat with jurisdiction over Yingtian Prefecture. The prefectural walls and ramparts were incomplete, and when bandits arrived the troops at last had no means to resist. Chengyou began by fortifying the southern pass, then dredged the Sha, Sui, and Meng rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Southern Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat with jurisdiction over Yingtian. The walls were incomplete, and when bandits came the garrison could not defend the city. Chengyou fortified the southern pass and dredged the Sha, Sui, and Meng rivers.

sentences.zh: 徙亳州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 諫官言承祐在應天府給糧不以次，且擅留糧綱，批宣頭，不發戍還兵，越法杖配輕罪，借用翰林器，出入擁旗槍，以禁兵同周衛，體涉狂僭，無人臣禮。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials said that at Yingtian Prefecture Chengyou issued grain out of order, moreover detained grain convoys on his own authority, annotated imperial rescripts, did not release garrison troops returning from duty, exceeded the law in beating and assigning light punishments, borrowed objects from the Hanlin, went in and out escorted by banners and spears, and used palace troops like the Zhou royal guard — his conduct smacked of arrogance and presumption and lacked the decorum of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials said that at Yingtian he issued grain out of order, detained grain convoys without authority, annotated imperial rescripts, refused to release returning garrison troops, exceeded the law in punishments, borrowed Hanlin objects, went about escorted by banners and spears, and used palace troops like a royal guard — conduct arrogant and presumptuous, unbecoming a subject.

sentences.zh: 罷宣徽南院使，許州都總管，徙節保靜軍、知許州。

translations.literal: He was removed as Southern Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, made Overall Commander of Xuzhou, and transferred to hold the seal of the Baojing Army while Acting Prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed as Southern Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, made Overall Commander of Xuzhou, and transferred to Military Governor of Baojing and Acting Prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 轉運使蘇舜元薦承祐有將帥才，政事如龔、黃。

translations.literal: The Transport Commissioner Su Shunyuan recommended that Chengyou had the talent of a general and that his administration was like that of Gong and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Su Shunyuan recommended Chengyou as having the talent of a general and compared his administration to that of Gong and Huang.

sentences.zh: 帝謂輔臣曰：「彼庸人，監司乃龔、黃比之，何所取信哉。

translations.literal: The emperor said to his chief ministers, "That mediocrity — and a supervisory official compares him to Gong and Huang. What is there to trust in that?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his chief ministers, "That mediocrity — and a supervisory official compares him to Gong and Huang. What is there to believe in that?"

sentences.zh: 」改知鄭州，未行，暴疾卒。

translations.literal: " He was changed to Acting Prefect of Zhengzhou, but before he set out he died suddenly of illness.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made Acting Prefect of Zhengzhou, but before he departed he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，謚曰密。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title Grand Commandant, with posthumous name Mi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant with the posthumous name Mi.

sentences.zh: 承祐所至，多興作為煩擾，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Wherever Chengyou went he launched many construction projects that became a nuisance, and the common people suffered from them.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Chengyou went he launched construction projects that harassed the people, and the common folk suffered under him.

sentences.zh: 李洪信

translations.literal: Li Hongxin
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongxin

sentences.zh: 晉初，為興順左廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin he was Commander of the Left Wing of the Xingshun Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Later Jin he was Commander of the Left Wing of the Xingshun Guard.

sentences.zh: 漢祖統禁軍，遷鎮太原，奏隸麾下。

translations.literal: When the Later Han founder took command of the Palace Guard and was transferred to garrison Taiyuan, Hongxin memorialized to be placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Han founder took command of the Palace Guard and was posted to Taiyuan, Hongxin asked to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 漢祖領陳州刺史、左護聖左廂都指揮使，俄加岳州防禦使。

translations.literal: The Later Han founder held the post of Prefect of Chenzhou and Commander of the Left Wing of the Left Sacred Guard, and soon Hongxin was additionally made Defender of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Han founder held Chenzhou and commanded the Left Wing of the Left Sacred Guard, and soon Hongxin was also made Defender of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 從漢祖降鄴，以警扈之勞，授侍衛馬軍都指揮使、領武信軍節度。

translations.literal: Following the Later Han founder in reducing Ye, for his labor in guard and escort he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Cavalry while holding the post of Military Governor of the Wuxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Han founder reduced Ye, Hongxin was rewarded for his service in guard and escort with the command of the Palace Cavalry and the Military Governorship of Wuxin.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，以群小用事，心懷憂懼，白太后求解軍職，出為鎮寧軍節度。

translations.literal: During Qianyou, because petty men held power he was anxious at heart, told the Empress Dowager he wished to be released from military office, and was sent out as Military Governor of the Zhenning Army.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyou, troubled that petty men held power, he asked the Empress Dowager to release him from military office and was sent out as Military Governor of Zhenning.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷保義軍節度。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Military Governor of the Baoyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was transferred to Military Governor of Baoyi.

sentences.zh: 初，楊邠以元從功臣為方鎮者，不諳政務，令三司擇軍將分補諸鎮都押牙、孔目官，或恃以朝選，藩帥難制。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Bin, because the founding followers who served as regional commanders were unversed in government affairs, ordered the Three Departments to select army officers to fill in succession the posts of Chief Military Adjutant and Clerical Officer in each commandery. Some relied on court selection, and the frontier governors found them hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Bin noted that founding followers serving as regional commanders were unversed in government. He had the Three Departments select army officers to fill the Chief Military Adjutant and Clerical Officer posts in each commandery. Some relied on court appointments, making them hard for the governors to control.

sentences.zh: 洪信聞內難，即召馬步軍都校聶召，奉國軍校楊德、王建、黃全武、楊進、翟本，右牙都校任溫、武德，護聖都校康審澄及判官路濤、掌書記張洞、都押牙楊昭𠡽、孔目官魏守恭，悉殺之，誣奏謀逆。

translations.literal: When Hongxin heard of the inner turmoil he at once summoned the Chief Commandant of the Horse and Foot Armies Nie Zhao, the Fengguo Guard officers Yang De, Wang Jian, Huang Quanwu, Yang Jin, and Zhai Ben, the Right Adjutant Commandants Ren Wen and Wu De, the Sacred Guard Commandant Kang Shencheng, and the Judge Lu Tao, Chief Secretary Zhang Dong, Chief Military Adjutant Yang Zhaohui, and Clerical Officer Wei Shougong — and had them all killed, then falsely memorialized that they had plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongxin heard of the court turmoil he summoned Chief Commandant Nie Zhao, Fengguo officers Yang De, Wang Jian, Huang Quanwu, Yang Jin, and Zhai Ben, Right Adjutant Commandants Ren Wen and Wu De, Sacred Guard Commandant Kang Shencheng, Judge Lu Tao, Chief Secretary Zhang Dong, Chief Military Adjutant Yang Zhaohui, and Clerical Officer Wei Shougong — and had them all killed, then falsely reported that they had plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 乾德五年，改左驍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiande he was changed to Grand General of the Left Valiant Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qiande he was made Grand General of the Left Valiant Guard.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年請老，以本官致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao he requested retirement and left office with his existing rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaibao he asked to retire and left office retaining his rank.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 洪信無他才術，徒以外戚致位將相。

translations.literal: Hongxin had no other talent or skill and reached the rank of general and minister solely through kinship by marriage with the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin had no real talent and reached the rank of general and minister solely as an imperial in-law.

sentences.zh: 斂財累鉅萬，而吝嗇尤甚。

translations.literal: He amassed wealth totaling tens of millions, yet was especially miserly.
translations.idiomatic: He amassed wealth in the tens of millions, yet was exceptionally miserly.

sentences.zh: 時節鎮皆廣置帳下親兵，惟洪信最寡少。

translations.literal: At that time every military governorship broadly maintained personal troops under its command, but Hongxin's were the fewest.
translations.idiomatic: At that time every military governorship maintained large personal retinues, but Hongxin's was the smallest.

sentences.zh: 弟洪義。

translations.literal: His younger brother Hongyi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Hongyi.

sentences.zh: 弟 洪義

translations.literal: Younger brother Hongyi
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Hongyi

sentences.zh: 洪義，本名洪威，避周祖名改焉。

translations.literal: Hongyi, original name Hongwei, changed it to avoid the taboo name of the Zhou founder.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyi, originally named Hongwei, changed his name to avoid the taboo of the Zhou founder's name.

sentences.zh: 漢祖鎮太原，補親校。

translations.literal: When the Later Han founder garrisoned Taiyuan, Hongyi was appointed to his personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Han founder held Taiyuan, Hongyi joined his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 開國，授護聖左廂都校、領岳州防禦使，遷侍衛馬軍都指揮使、領武信軍節度。

translations.literal: When the state was founded he was appointed Commander of the Left Wing of the Sacred Guard while holding the post of Defender of Yuezhou, then transferred to Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Cavalry while holding the post of Military Governor of the Wuxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the state was founded he was made Commander of the Left Wing of the Sacred Guard and Defender of Yuezhou, then Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Cavalry and Military Governor of Wuxin.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加兼中書令，移鄜州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was additionally made Chief Councillor of the Central Secretariat and transferred to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was also made Chief Councillor of the Central Secretariat and transferred to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德五年，代歸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiande he was replaced and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qiande he was relieved and returned to court.

sentences.zh: 卒年五十九，贈太師。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-nine and was posthumously given the title Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-nine and was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 武行德

translations.literal: Wu Xingde
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xingde

sentences.zh: 武行德，幷州榆次人，身長九尺餘，材貌奇偉，家甚貧，常采樵鬻之自給。

translations.literal: Wu Xingde was a native of Yuci in Bingzhou. His body was more than nine feet in height, his build and appearance extraordinarily imposing. His family was very poor, and he often gathered firewood and sold it to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xingde came from Yuci in Bingzhou. He stood more than nine feet tall, with an extraordinarily imposing build and bearing. His family was very poor, and he often gathered firewood to sell for a living.

sentences.zh: 晉祖鎮幷門，暇日，從禽郊外，值行德負薪趨拱於道左，晉祖見其魁岸，又所負薪異常，令力士更舉之，俱不能舉，頗奇之，因留帳下。

translations.literal: When the Later Jin founder garrisoned Bing Gate, on a leisure day he went hunting in the suburbs and encountered Xingde carrying firewood, hurrying to bow on the left of the road. The founder saw his towering stature and that the firewood he bore was unusual. He ordered strong men to try lifting it again, but none could raise it. He was quite struck by this and therefore kept Xingde in his personal following.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Jin founder held Bing Gate, on a day off he went hunting in the suburbs and saw Xingde carrying firewood, bowing by the roadside. The founder noted his towering stature and the extraordinary load of firewood. He had strong men try to lift it, but none could. Deeply impressed, he took Xingde into his personal service.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，授奉國都頭，遷指揮使，改控鶴指揮使、寧國軍都虞候。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianfu era of Jin he was appointed Head of the Fengguo Guard, promoted to Commander, then changed to Commander of the Crane Control Guard and Chief Commandant of the Ningguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianfu reign of Later Jin he was made Head of the Fengguo Guard, then Commander, then Commander of the Crane Control Guard and Chief Commandant of the Ningguo Army.

sentences.zh: 開運中，契丹至汴，行德被獲，乃偽請於契丹以自效。

translations.literal: During Kaiyun the Khitans reached Bian. Xingde was captured and then falsely requested of the Khitans that he might serve them.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyun the Khitans reached Bian. Xingde was captured and pretended to offer his service to them.

sentences.zh: 契丹信之，方具舟數十艘載鎧甲，令行德率將校軍卒送歸其國。

translations.literal: The Khitans trusted him. They had just prepared several dozen boats loaded with armor and ordered Xingde to lead officers and soldiers to escort them back to their country.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans trusted him. They had prepared several dozen boats loaded with armor and ordered Xingde to lead officers and soldiers to escort them home.

sentences.zh: 溯汴至河陰，行德謂諸將曰：「我輩受國厚恩，而受制於契丹，與其離鄉井、投邊塞，為異域之鬼，曷若與諸君驅逐兇黨，共守河陽，姑俟契丹兵退，視天命所屬歸之，建功業，定禍亂，以圖富貴可乎？

translations.literal: Sailing up the Bian to Heyin, Xingde said to the generals, "We have received profound favor from the state, yet are now controlled by the Khitans. Rather than leave our home villages, cast ourselves into the borderlands, and become ghosts in a foreign land, how much better to join you gentlemen in driving out these vicious partisans, holding Heyang together, waiting for the Khitan troops to withdraw, then seeing to whom Heaven's mandate belongs and submitting to him, establishing merit, settling turmoil, and seeking wealth and honor — would that not do?"
translations.idiomatic: Sailing up the Bian to Heyin, Xingde said to the officers, "We have received deep favor from our state, yet now serve the Khitans. Rather than leave our homes for the borderlands and die as ghosts in a foreign land, why not drive out these villains, hold Heyang together, wait for the Khitans to withdraw, then see whom Heaven favors, win merit, end the turmoil, and seek fortune and honor?"

sentences.zh: 」眾素服行德威名，皆曰：「所向惟命，不敢愛死。

translations.literal: " The men had long respected Xingde's martial renown and all said, "Wherever you lead we follow your command and dare not spare our lives."
translations.idiomatic: " The men had long respected Xingde's reputation and all said, "We follow your command wherever you lead and dare not spare our lives."

sentences.zh: 」行德即殺契丹監使，分授器甲，由汜水倍道抵河陽。

translations.literal: " Xingde at once killed the Khitan supervising envoy, distributed weapons and armor, and by the Sishui route marched at double speed to reach Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: " Xingde at once killed the Khitan supervisor, distributed arms and armor, and by the Sishui route marched at double speed to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 契丹節度使崔廷勳出兵來拒，行德麾眾逆擊，自旦及午殊死戰，廷勳大敗，棄城走。

translations.literal: The Khitan Military Governor Cui Tingxun led troops out to resist. Xingde commanded his men to strike back. From dawn until noon they fought a desperate battle. Tingxun was routed and abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan Military Governor Cui Tingxun marched out to resist. Xingde led his men to counterattack. From dawn until noon they fought a desperate battle. Tingxun was routed and fled, abandoning the city.

sentences.zh: 行德遂據河陽，盡以府庫分給將士，因推行德知州事。

translations.literal: Xingde then seized Heyang, distributed the entire prefectural treasury to officers and soldiers, and thereby had Xingde made Acting Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Xingde then held Heyang, distributed the entire prefectural treasury to his officers and soldiers, and was made Acting Prefect.

sentences.zh: 時契丹兵尚充斥，行德厲士卒，繕甲兵，據上遊，士氣益奮，人望歸之。

translations.literal: At that time Khitan troops still filled the region. Xingde roused his soldiers, repaired armor and weapons, held the upper reaches of the river, and morale grew ever more ardent as men's hopes turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Khitans still filled the region. Xingde roused his troops, repaired arms and armor, held the upper river, and morale soared as the people looked to him.

sentences.zh: 聞漢祖起太原，即自稱河陽都部署，遣其弟行友間道奉表勸進，漢祖覽奏喜甚，即授行德河陽三城節度。

translations.literal: Hearing that the Later Han founder had risen at Taiyuan, he at once styled himself Overall Commander of Heyang, sent his younger brother Xingyou by a hidden route to present a memorial urging him to take the throne, and when the founder read the memorial he was greatly pleased and at once appointed Xingde Military Governor of the Three Cities of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the Later Han founder had risen at Taiyuan, he styled himself Overall Commander of Heyang and sent his brother Xingyou by a hidden route with a memorial urging him to take the throne. The founder was delighted and at once made Xingde Military Governor of the Three Cities of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 漢祖由晉、絳至洛，行德迎候境上，以所部兵翼至京師，還河陽。

translations.literal: When the Later Han founder went from Jin and Jiang to Luoyang, Xingde met and welcomed him at the border, brought his command in support to the capital, then returned to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Han founder went from Jin and Jiang to Luoyang, Xingde met him at the border, escorted his troops to the capital, then returned to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，加同平章事，移真定尹、成德軍節度。

translations.literal: During Qianyou he was given the additional title of Co-Grand Councillor and transferred to be Governor of Zhending and Military Governor of the Chengde Army.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyou he was made Co-Grand Councillor and transferred to Governor of Zhending and Military Governor of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，加兼侍中，俄改忠武軍節度，遷河南尹、西京留守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was additionally made Palace Attendant, then soon changed to Military Governor of the Zhongwu Army and transferred to be Governor of Henan and Western Capital Regent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangshun he was also made Palace Attendant, then soon made Military Governor of Zhongwu and Governor of Henan and Regent of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 時禁鹽入城，犯者法至死，告者給厚賞。

translations.literal: At that time bringing salt into the city was forbidden. Violators were by law punished with death, and informants were given rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bringing salt into the city was forbidden on pain of death, and informants received rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 洛陽民家嫗將入城鬻蔬，俄有僧從嫗買蔬，就筥翻視，密置鹽筥中，少答其直，不買而去。

translations.literal: An old woman of a Luoyang household was about to enter the city to sell vegetables. Suddenly a monk came from the woman to buy vegetables, leaned over her basket and turned the contents to look, secretly placed salt in the basket, paid her less than the price, and left without buying.
translations.idiomatic: An old woman of Luoyang was about to enter the city to sell vegetables. A monk came to buy from her, leaned over her basket and secretly placed salt in it, paid her less than the price, and left without buying.

sentences.zh: 嫗持入城，抱關者搜得鹽，擒以詣府。

translations.literal: The woman carried it into the city. The gate guards searched and found salt, seized her, and brought her to the government office.
translations.idiomatic: She carried the basket into the city. The gate guards found the salt, seized her, and brought her to the magistrate.

sentences.zh: 行德見盛鹽襆非村嫗所有，疑而詰之，嫗言：「適有僧自城外買蔬，取視久之而去。

translations.literal: Xingde saw that the bundle of salt was not something a village woman would possess, grew suspicious, and questioned her. The woman said, "Just now a monk from outside the city came to buy vegetables from me, looked them over for a long time, and then left."
translations.idiomatic: Xingde saw that the bundle of salt was not something a village woman would own, questioned her, and she said, "A monk from outside the city just came to buy vegetables, looked them over for a long time, and left."

sentences.zh: 」即捕僧訊治之，具狀與關吏同誣以希賞。

translations.literal: " He at once seized the monk and interrogated him. The full account showed that he and the gate officer together had framed her in hope of reward.
translations.idiomatic: " He seized the monk and interrogated him. The full account showed that he and the gate officer had framed her together to claim the reward.

sentences.zh: 行德釋嫗，斬僧及抱關吏數輩。

translations.literal: Xingde released the woman and beheaded the monk and several gate officers.
translations.idiomatic: Xingde released the woman and beheaded the monk and several gate officers.

sentences.zh: 人畏之若神明，部下凜然。

translations.literal: People feared him as they would a spirit, and his subordinates were sternly awed.
translations.idiomatic: People feared him as they would a god, and his subordinates stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 三年，丁外艱，起復。

translations.literal: In the third year, when his father died, he was recalled from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, after his father's death, he was recalled from mourning.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加中書令，進封韓國公，再授忠武軍節度，改封魏國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was given the title Chief Councillor of the Central Secretariat, advanced and enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Han, again appointed Military Governor of the Zhongwu Army, and changed in enfeoffment to Duke of the State of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made Chief Councillor of the Central Secretariat, promoted to Duke of Han, again made Military Governor of Zhongwu, and then enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，冬，移鎮安州，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande, in winter, he was transferred to garrison Anzhou and given the rank of Opening the Government with the Insignia of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Qiande he was transferred to Anzhou and granted the rank of Opening the Government with the Insignia of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，入為太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he entered service as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he was appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，以本官致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he retired from office with his existing rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he retired retaining his rank.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年七十二，贈太師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged seventy-two, and was posthumously given the title Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died at the age of seventy-two and was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 楊承信

translations.literal: Yang Chengxin
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chengxin

sentences.zh: 楊承信，字守真，其先沙陀部人。

translations.literal: Yang Chengxin, style name Shouzhen, was by ancestry a man of the Shatuo tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chengxin, style name Shouzhen, was descended from the Shatuo tribe.

sentences.zh: 父光遠，仕晉至太師、壽王。

translations.literal: His father Guangyuan served Jin to the rank of Grand Preceptor and Prince of Shou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guangyuan served Later Jin to the rank of Grand Preceptor and Prince of Shou.

sentences.zh: 承信，光遠第二子，幼以父任，自義武軍節院使領蘭州刺史，歷宣武、平盧二軍牙校。

translations.literal: Chengxin was Guangyuan's second son. In youth through his father's position he began as Commissioner of the Yiwu Army Bureau while holding the post of Prefect of Lanzhou, and served in succession as adjutant in the Xuanwu and Pinglu armies.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxin was Guangyuan's second son. Through his father's influence in youth he became Commissioner of the Yiwu Army Bureau and Prefect of Lanzhou, then served as adjutant in the Xuanwu and Pinglu armies.

sentences.zh: 開運初，光遠以青州叛，少帝遣李守貞等討之，食盡勢窮，承信兄承勳劫其父以降，青州平，光遠死。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun, Guangyuan rebelled with Qingzhou. The young emperor sent Li Shouzhen and others to campaign against him. When food was exhausted and their situation desperate, Chengxin's elder brother Chengxun seized their father to force surrender. Qingzhou was pacified and Guangyuan died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyun, Guangyuan rebelled and held Qingzhou. The young emperor sent Li Shouzhen and others against him. When supplies ran out and defeat was near, Chengxin's elder brother Chengxun seized their father to force surrender. Qingzhou fell and Guangyuan was killed.

sentences.zh: 承信與弟承祚詣闕請死，詔釋之，以承信為右羽林將軍，承祚為右驍衛將軍，放歸，服喪私第，尋安置鄭州。
