translations.literal: Chengxin and his younger brother Chengzuo went to court to request death. An edict released them. Chengxin was made General of the Right Feathered Forest Guard and Chengzuo General of the Right Valiant Guard. They were sent home, observed mourning in their private residence, and soon were settled at Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxin and his brother Chengzuo went to court to ask for death. An edict pardoned them. Chengxin was made General of the Right Feathered Forest Guard and Chengzuo General of the Right Valiant Guard. They were sent home to mourn in their private residence and soon settled at Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，光遠送款契丹求援，兵未至而光遠降。

translations.literal: Earlier, Guangyuan had offered allegiance to the Khitans to seek aid, but before their troops arrived Guangyuan had surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Guangyuan had submitted to the Khitans for aid, but before their troops arrived he had already surrendered.

sentences.zh: 及契丹來寇，承勳時為鄭州防禦使，召數其罪殺之。

translations.literal: When the Khitans came to raid, Chengxun was then Defender of Zhengzhou. He summoned Guangyuan, recounted his crimes, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans invaded, Chengxun was Defender of Zhengzhou. He summoned Guangyuan, recounted his crimes, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 以承信為平戶軍節度，繼父職。

translations.literal: Chengxin was made Military Governor of the Pinghu Army, succeeding his father's post.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxin was made Military Governor of Pinghu, succeeding his father's post.

sentences.zh: 仕漢歷安、鄜二州節度，累加檢校太師。

translations.literal: Serving Han, he held in succession the military governorships of An and Fu, and was repeatedly given the additional title of Acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Han he served in turn as Military Governor of An and Fu and was repeatedly made Acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 承信身長八尺，美儀表，善持論，且多藝能，雖叛臣之子，然累歷藩鎮，刻勵為政而不苛，故能始終富貴。

translations.literal: Chengxin was eight feet in height, of fine bearing, skilled at discourse, and moreover had many talents. Though he was the son of a rebel minister, he served repeatedly in frontier commands, applied himself diligently in government without harshness, and therefore was able to remain wealthy and honored to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxin stood eight feet tall, with a fine bearing, skilled in debate and accomplished in many arts. Though the son of a rebel minister, he served repeatedly on the frontier, governed diligently without harshness, and thus remained wealthy and honored to the end.

sentences.zh: 其卒也，蒲民表乞祠之，則其遺愛之在人者，可知矣。

translations.literal: When he died, the people of Pu submitted a memorial requesting a shrine to him — from this one may know how his lingering kindness toward the people endured.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the people of Pu petitioned for a shrine in his honor — showing how his kindness was remembered.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，錄其孫松為奉職。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde his grandson Song was enrolled as a Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jingde his grandson Song was enrolled as a Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 侯章，幷州榆次人。

translations.literal: Hou Zhang was a native of Yuci in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhang came from Yuci in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初在幷門事後唐莊宗為隊長，明宗朝遷小校。

translations.literal: At first he served at Bing Gate under the Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong as squad leader, and in the Mingzong reign was promoted to junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: He first served at Bing Gate under Later Tang Zhuangzong as squad leader and was promoted to junior officer under Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 晉開運末，為忠衛指揮使，屯兵陜州，為內外馬步軍都指揮使兼三城巡檢使。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyun era of Jin he was Commander of the Loyal Guard, garrisoned troops at Shaanzhou, and was made Commander-in-Chief of the Inner and Outer Horse and Foot Armies while also serving as Patrol Commissioner of the Three Cities.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Kaiyun reign of Later Jin he commanded the Loyal Guard, garrisoned Shaanzhou, and was made Commander-in-Chief of the Inner and Outer Horse and Foot Armies and Patrol Commissioner of the Three Cities.

sentences.zh: 會契丹入中原，與趙暉、王晏謀斬契丹將劉愿，送款於漢祖。

translations.literal: When the Khitans entered the Central Plains, he plotted with Zhao Hui and Wang Yan to behead the Khitan general Liu Yuan and offer allegiance to the Later Han founder.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans entered the Central Plains, he joined Zhao Hui and Wang Yan in plotting to kill the Khitan general Liu Yuan and submit to the Later Han founder.

sentences.zh: 漢祖入汴，擢為鎮國軍節度。

translations.literal: When the Later Han founder entered Bian, Zhang was promoted to Military Governor of the Zhenguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Han founder entered Bian, Zhang was promoted to Military Governor of Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，加同平章事，尋移鎮邠州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou he was given the additional title of Co-Grand Councillor, then soon transferred to garrison Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianyou he was made Co-Grand Councillor, then soon transferred to Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 章居鎮無善政，傲上剝下，以貪猥聞，用見戶為逃，擅其租賦，乃矯奏貧民數千戶負稅租，久禁繫不能輸，願以己俸代。

translations.literal: In his commandery Zhang had no good government. He was arrogant toward superiors and exploited subordinates, and was known for greed and baseness. He treated visible households as fugitives and seized their rents and taxes. He then falsely memorialized that several thousand poor households owed tax and rent, had long been imprisoned and unable to pay, and that he wished to substitute his own salary on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: In his commandery Zhang governed badly. He was arrogant toward superiors and exploited subordinates, and was known for greed and corruption. He treated registered households as fugitives and seized their taxes. He then falsely reported that several thousand poor households owed taxes, had long been imprisoned unable to pay, and offered to cover the debt from his own salary.

sentences.zh: 時方姑息，詔褒之。

translations.literal: The court was then indulgent and conciliatory, and an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then in an indulgent mood and issued an edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 副使趙彥鐸有良馬，章欲之不與，誣彥鐸謀逆之，殺之，亦置而不問。

translations.literal: The deputy commissioner Zhao Yanduo had a fine horse. Zhang wanted it but Yanduo would not give it. Zhang falsely accused Yanduo of plotting rebellion and killed him, yet this too was set aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Commissioner Zhao Yanduo had a fine horse. Zhang wanted it but Yanduo refused. Zhang falsely accused him of plotting rebellion and killed him, and this too went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 俄加檢校太師。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made Acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 論曰：王景輩微時，或至為盜、負薪，遭五代之亂，奮身戎功，重據邊要。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Wang Jing and his kind in humble times sometimes became bandits or carried firewood. Encountering the chaos of the Five Dynasties, they threw themselves into military achievement and repeatedly held weighty frontier posts.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Men like Wang Jing in humble times sometimes became bandits or gathered firewood. In the chaos of the Five Dynasties they threw themselves into military service and repeatedly held important frontier posts.

sentences.zh: 宋興，稽顙北嚮，太祖待以誠信，宜無不自安者。

translations.literal: When Song arose they bowed their foreheads to the north. Taizu treated them with sincerity and trust, and they ought all to have felt secure.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song arose they bowed to the north. Taizu treated them with sincerity and trust, and they ought all to have felt secure.

sentences.zh: 景趨利改圖，乃至滅族。

translations.literal: Yet Jing, seeking profit, changed his allegiance, and in the end his clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Jing turned for profit and shifted his allegiance, his clan was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 王晏、郭從義遷怒肆忿，誣人以死。

translations.literal: Wang Yan and Guo Congyi shifted their anger and vented their rage, framing men and putting them to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan and Guo Congyi vented their anger on others and framed men to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 侯章在藩邸有剝下之名，李洪義狃於肺腑之戚，而無外凜之志，咎孰甚焉！

translations.literal: Hou Zhang in his commandery had a reputation for exploiting subordinates. Li Hongyi clung to kinship of flesh and blood yet lacked outward awe toward authority — whose fault was the greater!
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhang was known in his commandery for exploiting subordinates. Li Hongyi relied on imperial kinship but lacked proper respect for authority — whose fault was worse!

sentences.zh: 斯皆亂世之習，有不能盡去之者。

translations.literal: These were all habits of a chaotic age, and there were some that could not be entirely cast off.
translations.idiomatic: These were habits of a chaotic age that could not be entirely cast off.

sentences.zh: 武行德守洛邑，辯究欺罔，民用畏服，顧不優於諸人耶？

translations.literal: Wu Xingde held Luoyang, investigated and exposed deception, and the people in consequence feared and submitted to him — was he not after all superior to the others?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xingde held Luoyang, investigated fraud, and made the people fear and respect him — was he not superior to the rest?
